sources.ref_file_title: Aar05 - Quantum computing, postselection, and probabilistic polynomial-time
sources.venue: Proceedings of the Royal Society A 461(2063), pp. 3473-3482
sources.note: PostBQP = PP; also arXiv quant-ph/0412187. Verified at royalsocietypublishing.org.

pages.class_justification: Unconditional, proven complexity-class inclusion; the repo convention (cf. bpp-to-pspace) types proven containments as free.
pages.model_justification: The theorem itself is unconditional classical mathematics, but the repo convention marks containments involving quantum classes with model: quantum (cf. bpp-to-bqp, qcma-to-pp, qma-to-pp); kept for consistency.
pages.statement: $\classBQP \subseteq \classPP$: every language decidable with bounded error by a polynomial-time quantum algorithm ([[bounded-error-quantum-polynomial-time|BQP]]) lies in [[probabilistic-polynomial-time|PP]] — [[ADH97 - Quantum Computability|ADH97]]. The containment also follows from $\mathsf{PostBQP} = \classPP$ — [[Aar05 - Quantum computing, postselection, and probabilistic polynomial-time|Aar05]].
pages.sketch: Writing the acceptance probability of a quantum circuit as a sum over computation paths of products of (rational) amplitudes expresses it as the difference of two $\classsharpP$ functions; deciding whether this GapP value exceeds the acceptance threshold is exactly a $\classPP$ predicate.
pages.improvements_text: - $\mathsf{PostBQP} = \classPP$ gives a simpler alternative proof of the containment — [[Aar05 - Quantum computing, postselection, and probabilistic polynomial-time|Aar05]]
flags: probabilistic-polynomial-time.md (Known relationships) carries a 'TODO citation (Adleman, DeMarrais, Huang 1997)' for this same fact; the new ADH97 reference page resolves it — same-commit cleanup opportunity for the reference-fixer lane.

pages.wrong_reason: As stated (CDH hard ⇒ BDH hard), this is not a known theorem in any model. The trivial known direction is the converse: a CDH solver in the base group breaks BDH — from $g^a, g^b$ compute $g^{ab}$, then $e(g^{ab}, g^c) = e(g,g)^{abc}$ — so BDH hardness implies CDH hardness (BDH ⇒ CDH). The migrated bullet's 'BDH is implied by CDH in the generic group model' misreads the unconditional generic-bilinear-group lower bound for BDH (a hardness proof in an idealized model, quantifying over all generic algorithms) as a reduction from CDH; the suspected-errors entry for bilinear-map-assumptions.md line 35 flags exactly this. Correct edge: bdh-to-cdh.
flags: No inverse page bdh-to-cdh exists in content/Reductions/ — worth creating (folklore, fully-black-box: one pairing evaluation turns a base-group CDH solver into a BDH solver).

The unconditional generic-group hardness of BDH is a different fact (a model-scoped lower bound, not an edge from CDH); if wanted it belongs on the assumption page or as a barrier-style note, not as this reduction.

pages.wrong_reason: Direction inverted. The true implication is DDH ⇒ CDH: a CDH solver computes $g^{ab}$ from $(g, g^a, g^b)$ and compares it with the challenge element, breaking DDH, so DDH hardness implies CDH hardness. No converse reduction is known, and none can be group-generic: in symmetric pairing groups DDH is easy while CDH is conjectured hard (Joux–Nguyen gap groups). The migrated sentence contradicts its own following gloss, as the suspected-errors entry for decisional-diffie-hellman.md line 12 records. The correct edge already exists as content/Reductions/ddh-to-cdh.md.
flags: Recommend deleting or redirecting this page: ddh-to-cdh.md already covers the true direction, so repairing in place would create a duplicate.
computational-diffie-hellman.md line 12 and decisional-diffie-hellman.md line 12 carry the mirrored prose confusion — skeptical-checker lane.

pages.class_justification: The reduction is fixed in advance and treats the DLOG solver only as an oracle: on a CDH instance it makes a single oracle call to recover an exponent and finishes with one exponentiation in the same group. No dependence on the solver's code, no change of instance distribution.
pages.statement: If [[computational-diffie-hellman|CDH]] is hard in a group family, then [[discrete-logarithm|DLOG]] is hard in the same family: any efficient algorithm computing discrete logarithms yields an efficient CDH solver, so the DLOG assumption is the weaker of the two — folklore.
pages.sketch: Given a CDH instance $(g, g^a, g^b)$, run the DLOG solver on $(g, g^a)$ to obtain $a$ and output $(g^b)^a$. A single discrete-log call suffices — $g^a$ is a uniformly random group element in both games — and the reduction succeeds exactly when the solver does.
flags: The edge is true as stated, but the source prose (discrete-logarithm.md line 12, 'DLOG is a natural strengthening of the CDH assumption') inverts assumption strength — suspected-errors entry stands; skeptical-checker lane.
The migrated sketch invoked two DLOG calls (on g^x and g^y); one suffices, as the new sketch records.

sources.ref_file_title: HLL23 - Attribute-Based Encryption for Circuits of Unbounded Depth from Lattices Garbled Circuits of Optimal Size, Laconic Functional Evaluation, and More
sources.authors: Yao-Ching Hsieh, Huijia Lin, Ji Luo
sources.note: Introduces the evasive circular LWE assumption and builds ABE/PE for circuits of unbounded depth and size from it. Journal version in SIAM J. Comput. (DOI 10.1137/24M1629316). Verified via eprint listing and FOCS record.

sources.ref_file_title: AMYY25 - Evasive LWE Attacks, Variants & Obfustopia
sources.authors: Shweta Agrawal, Anuja Modi, Anshu Yadav, Shota Yamada
sources.note: NOT an improvement of the reduction: it is the attack on the hypothesis (a sampler for which circular evasive LWE's pre-condition holds but its post-condition fails). Listed here only because the statement cites it; do not render it in an improvements section.

pages.class_justification: The hypothesis is an implication-style lattice assumption (quantified over samplers), not a primitive used as an oracle; the RTV taxonomy does not apply and HLL23 do not classify the reduction. Honest value: unstated.
pages.statement: Assuming the public-coin circular variant of [[learning-with-errors#evasive-lwe|evasive LWE]] (evasive circular LWE), there is a lattice-based [[attribute-based-encryption|ABE]] scheme for circuits of unbounded depth and size — [[HLL23 - Attribute-Based Encryption for Circuits of Unbounded Depth from Lattices Garbled Circuits of Optimal Size, Laconic Functional Evaluation, and More|HLL23]]. [[AMYY25 - Evasive LWE Attacks, Variants & Obfustopia|AMYY25]] exhibit a sampler for which the assumption's pre-condition holds but its post-condition fails, so the hypothesis is contested.
notes_to_keep: The hypothesis assumption (circular evasive LWE) has a published counterexample sampler — [[AMYY25 - Evasive LWE Attacks, Variants & Obfustopia|AMYY25]]; the edge is a conditional theorem whose hypothesis is contested.
flags: Page title says 'Evasive LWE ⇒ ABE' but the frontmatter hypothesis is circular-evasive-lwe; retitle to 'Circular evasive LWE ⇒ ABE' (and consider a -hll23 slug suffix) to distinguish from evasive-lwe-to-abe-wee22.
The migration note suggesting a 'refuted'/'contested-hypothesis' status marker remains a fair schema question for a human; the reduction itself stands as a conditional theorem.
HLL23 also builds PE, laconic functional evaluation, 1-key FE and reusable garbling from the same assumption — candidate additional edges, not recorded here.

sources.ref_file_title: BV11 - Efficient Fully Homomorphic Encryption from (Standard) LWE
sources.note: First FHE from plain LWE (leveled unconditionally under LWE; unbounded FHE under the additional circular-security assumption). DOI 10.1109/FOCS.2011.12. Verified via eprint and IEEE/ACM records.

sources.ref_file_title: BGV12 - Leveled fully homomorphic encryption without bootstrapping
sources.authors: Zvika Brakerski, Craig Gentry, Vinod Vaikuntanathan

sources.ref_file_title: GSW13 - Homomorphic Encryption from Learning with Errors Conceptually-Simpler, Asymptotically-Faster, Attribute-Based
sources.authors: Craig Gentry, Amit Sahai, Brent Waters
sources.note: Approximate-eigenvector FHE from LWE; no relinearization keys. Springer DOI 10.1007/978-3-642-40041-4_5. Verified via eprint and Springer records.

pages.class_justification: The hypotheses are assumptions (LWE, and circular security of the constructed scheme itself — a self-referential property), not primitives used as oracles, and the unbounded variant bootstraps by evaluating the scheme's own decryption circuit; no source assigns an RTV class.
pages.statement: Assuming the hardness of [[learning-with-errors|LWE]], there is a leveled fully homomorphic encryption scheme; assuming in addition [[circular-security|circular security]] — the scheme remains secure when publishing encryptions of its own secret key — bootstrapping yields [[homomorphic-encryption|FHE]] for circuits of arbitrary depth — [[BV11 - Efficient Fully Homomorphic Encryption from (Standard) LWE|BV11]].
pages.sketch: BV11 build an LWE-based scheme whose homomorphic multiplication uses relinearization (key switching) and whose noise growth is tamed by dimension-modulus reduction; publishing encryptions of the secret key (circular security) enables Gentry-style bootstrapping, which refreshes ciphertext noise by homomorphically evaluating the decryption circuit.
pages.improvements_text:
- Leveled FHE from LWE with better noise management via modulus switching, removing bootstrapping for bounded-depth circuits — [[BGV12 - Leveled fully homomorphic encryption without bootstrapping|BGV12]]
- Conceptually simpler FHE from LWE via the approximate-eigenvector method, with no relinearization keys — [[GSW13 - Homomorphic Encryption from Learning with Errors Conceptually-Simpler, Asymptotically-Faster, Attribute-Based|GSW13]]
flags: The migrated quote's 'Current constructions all rely on lattice assumptions' is false (FHE also from iO-based routes etc.) — already recorded in migration notes; drop with the boilerplate.
content/Assumptions/circular-security.md now exists; the migration note claiming 'circular-security has no wiki page' is outdated.

sources.ref_file_title: Gen09 - Fully homomorphic encryption using ideal lattices

pages.class_justification: The transformation feeds the scheme's own decryption circuit to $\Eval$: the construction depends on the hypothesis scheme's code, not merely oracle access, so it is not fully-black-box; neither Gen09 nor follow-up work places it in an RTV class. Honest value: unstated.
pages.statement: Any bootstrappable [[homomorphic-encryption#somewhat-homomorphic-encryption-she|somewhat homomorphic encryption]] scheme — one able to homomorphically evaluate its own augmented decryption circuit — with [[circular-security|circular security]] yields [[homomorphic-encryption|FHE]] for circuits of arbitrary depth (Gentry's bootstrapping theorem) — [[Gen09 - Fully homomorphic encryption using ideal lattices|Gen09]]. Without circular security the transformation gives only leveled FHE, using a chain of independent key pairs.
pages.sketch: The public key includes encryptions of the secret key. To refresh a noisy ciphertext $c$, homomorphically evaluate the decryption circuit $\Dec(\cdot, c)$ on the encrypted secret key, producing a fresh encryption of the same plaintext with bounded noise; interleaving a refresh with each gate evaluates circuits of any depth.
notes_to_keep: The SHE hypothesis anchors to a section of the same page as the conclusion (homomorphic-encryption.md), so the edge renders as a near self-loop until SHE gets its own page.
flags: Bootstrappability is a genuine extra hypothesis on the SHE scheme; it is stated in the statement text but is not capturable in the hypothesis list — schema question flagged during migration remains.
The migration REPAIR PATCH note (attaching the circular-security bullet to this chain) is resolved by the statement above; the remaining migration boilerplate can be dropped.

sources.ref_file_title: BLS01 - Short Signatures from the Weil Pairing
sources.authors: Dan Boneh, Ben Lynn, Hovav Shacham
sources.note: BLS signatures; EUF-CMA in the ROM in gap (co-)Diffie-Hellman groups. Verified via Springer and iacr.org archive.

sources.ref_file_title: BLS04 - Short Signatures from the Weil Pairing (Journal of Cryptology)
sources.authors: Dan Boneh, Ben Lynn, Hovav Shacham
sources.note: Journal version with the general co-GDH framework and the asymmetric-pairing co-CDH formulation. Same title as BLS01; filename disambiguated with venue suffix.

pages.class_justification: Fixed construction using only group, hash, and pairing operations; the security reduction runs the forger once as an oracle, programming its random oracle, and extracts a co-CDH solution from the forgery. Standard fully-black-box shape, in the ROM.
pages.model_justification: Security is proved with $H$ modeled as a random oracle (BLS01 Theorem for gap co-DH groups); no standard-model proof is known.
pages.statement: BLS signatures: in bilinear groups $(\GG_1, \GG_2)$ with pairing $e$ and hash $H : \bits^* \to \GG_1$ modeled as a random oracle, the secret key is $x$, the public key is $g_2^x$, and $\Sign(x, m) = H(m)^x$; verification checks $e(\sigma, g_2) = e(H(m), \pk)$. The scheme is EUF-CMA secure under [[co-computational-diffie-hellman|co-CDH]] in the random-oracle model — [[BLS01 - Short Signatures from the Weil Pairing|BLS01]].
pages.sketch: The reduction sets $\pk = g_2^a$ from the co-CDH challenge $(g_2^a, h)$ and programs the random oracle: most hash values are $g_1^{r}$ with known $r$, so signing queries are answerable from $\psi(g_2^a)^r$, while an occasional value is $h \cdot g_1^{r}$; a forgery on such a point yields $h^a$, solving co-CDH.
pages.improvements_text: - Journal version with the general co-GDH framework and the asymmetric-pairing co-CDH formulation — [[BLS04 - Short Signatures from the Weil Pairing (Journal of Cryptology)|BLS04]]
flags: content/Assumptions/co-computational-diffie-hellman.md now exists; the migration note claiming co-CDH has no page is outdated.
Security loss is the Coron-style factor ~e(q_s+1) over the co-CDH advantage; left blank pending verification against the theorem statement in BLS01/BLS04.

pages.wrong_reason: GMW87's semi-honest protocol is built from oblivious transfer, not from commitments; commitments (via zero-knowledge proofs for NP) enter only in the GMW compiler lifting semi-honest security to malicious security. As stated, 'COM is complete for MPC in the semi-honest model' is false: commitments follow from OWFs (Naor from PRG/HILL), semi-honest 2PC implies OT, and OT is black-box separated from OWFs (Impagliazzo-Rudich), so the claim would collapse Minicrypt into Cryptomania. The suspected-errors entries for commitment-scheme.md line 64 and secure-multi-party-computation.md line 64 record the same error. Correct GMW87-adjacent edges: OT ⇒ semi-honest MPC (GMW87), and {ZK-from-COM, semi-honest MPC} ⇒ malicious MPC (the GMW compiler) — neither is what this page states.
flags: The citation GMW87 is real but attached to a claim the paper does not make; consider replacing this page with an ot-to-mpc-gmw87 edge and a separate GMW-compiler edge rather than repairing in place.
content/Reductions/ot-to-mpc-kil88.md already covers OT-completeness via Kilian; check for overlap before creating a GMW87 OT edge.

pages.wrong_reason: Inverted citation. Kil88 ('Founding cryptography on oblivious transfer') proves OT is complete for secure two-party computation — everything, commitments included, can be built from OT — not that OT can be built from commitments. A classical OT-from-COM construction would place OT in Minicrypt (commitments follow from OWFs) and contradict the Impagliazzo-Rudich black-box separation. The suspected-errors entry for commitment-scheme.md line 65 records this. Correct edges already exist: content/Reductions/ot-to-com.md and content/Reductions/ot-to-mpc-kil88.md. (In the quantum model, OT from commitments is achievable — Crépeau-Kilian FOCS 1988 / BBCS92 — a different, true statement this standard-model page does not make.)
